monthly_review.summary: Pace improved significantly this month while volume increased, but aerobic TE rose and cadence dropped — suggesting fatigue or form compromise despite faster running.
monthly_review.highlight: The 33-sec/km pace improvement (501 → 534 sec/km) coincides with a +7 bpm average HR, +0.3% aerobic TE, and +0.49 ml/kg/km efficiency decline — indicating the faster pace was achieved at higher physiological cost, consistent with a real trend across three prior months (July–September showing rising HR and efficiency deterioration).

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already exceeded last month’s distance (61.1 vs 51.3 km) and run count (12 vs 10) with 7 days remaining — no additional volume is needed. Given missing recovery data and signs of metabolic strain (rising HR, declining efficiency), chasing further volume would be inadvisable.

insights.title: Pace–HR dissociation suggests compromised aerobic economy
insights.body: Avg pace improved by 33 sec/km while avg HR rose +7 bpm and aerobic TE increased +0.3% — indicating reduced cardiovascular efficiency at faster paces, corroborated by worsening running economy (14.12 → 14.61 ml/kg/km) over two months.

insights.title: Cadence drop aligns with elevated vertical oscillillation
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 144 spm (Sep), while recent runs show vertical oscillillation consistently ≥8.1 cm (e.g., 8.6 cm on 2026-09-24) — higher than July’s 6.9 cm on 2026-09-06 — suggesting less efficient force transfer and possible fatigue-induced bounce.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance masks under-recovery
insights.body: Zone 3 share jumped from 26% (Aug) to 30% (Sep), while Z1 dropped from 43% to 20% — a 23-point shift toward threshold work without corresponding recovery metrics, increasing risk of cumulative fatigue despite no VO2max or decoupling data being available.

recommendations.action: Zone 2 run, HR ≤135 bpm, 5.0 km, Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Re-establish aerobic base without adding strain; current avg HR is 141 bpm and rising, so strict HR cap prevents further TE/efficiency degradation.

recommendations.action: Complete 20 min post-run mobility routine (focus: hip flexors, calves, thoracic rotation) after every run this week
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillillation increased +1.7 cm from Sept 6 (6.9 cm) to Sept 24 (8.6 cm), indicating stiffness or neuromuscular fatigue that mobility can mitigate.

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 4+ efforts this week; replace planned interval session with 4 × 2-min strides at 5:00/km with full 90-sec walk recovery
recommendations.reason: Zone 4 share rose to 22% (Sep) from 8% (Aug) while recovery metrics are absent — strides maintain neuromuscular sharpness without systemic load.

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic TE increased from 2.6% (Aug) to 2.9% (Sep); recent long run (2026-09-06) showed 5.0% TE — above 5% threshold — with no recovery data to confirm resilience
risk_flags.action: Monitor next long run TE; if ≥4.5%, reduce duration by 20% and add 2 min Z1 cooldown.
